4.text: may send their “spirits” to a destined place, but also may turn themselves

5.text: into any of their “spirits,” and carry out their intentions, appears in many tales.

6.text: For instance, in the tale of the Shaman with Warts (Kukuˊlpin), this

7.text: shaman, during a shamanistic contest, asks his adversary, “Which keˊlᴇ are you

8.text: going to employ?” The other answers, “The small hawk.” — “And you?” —

9.text: “The great diver.” Then they turn into these birds, and the contest begins.¹

19.text: There followed the leather bucket, which forms a part of a “bone-

20.text: breaking set,” and is used as a receptacle for pounded bones.² Once when

21.text: Scratching-Woman was hunting wild reindeer, he succeeded in wounding a

22.text: strong buck in the right fore-leg, but still he could not overtake it. Then

23.text: he called for the Skin Bucket, bade it overtake the buck and entrap its head.

24.text: After that the reindeer was easily caught.

25.text: After having entered the room and produced a few sounds, by way of

26.text: making his presence known, the “spirit” usually offers to “try his breath;”

27.text: that is, he beats the drum for a while, singing a tune in the special harsh

28.text: voice peculiar to the “spirits.” This, however, lasts only a short time, after

29.text: which the “spirit” declares that his breath is ebbing away. Then he either

30.text: begins to talk, or straightway takes his departure with characteristic quivering

31.text: sounds somewhat similar to the buzzing of a fly. These sounds are called

32.text: by the Chukchee “gibbering” (moomg̣aˊtɪrg̣ɪn), and are always associated

33.text: with the “spirits.” The same name is applied to the chattering alluded to

35.text: Often the shaman declares to the “spirit” first entering, that the sound

36.text: of his drum is bad, or even that the cover of it is broken, and this is cor-

37.text: roborated by a few dull strokes. The “spirit” must then mend the drum by

38.text: breathing upon it, which he does accordingly. This treatment is resorted to

39.text: especially in cases of magic medicine. After the drum is mended, the shaman

40.text: explains to the patient that it is a good sign. He says also, that, if the “spirit”

41.text: were not able to mend the drum, it would forebode a bad turn in the disease.
